newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Port Adelaide coach John Cahill and operations manager Mick Moylan are both expected to retain their jobs despite a very public conflict this week. The problems between the two are said to be administrative and not personal, and it is hoped they can be solved without any job casualties. Page 20.

Former Auckland backline general Grant Fox has denied the Auckland side will go into Saturday's Rugby Union Super 12 final with an air of complacency, saying the ACT Brumbies are one rival the Auckland side respects most. The last time the sides clashed Auckland won convincingly, 41-29. Page 19.

Socceroo goalkeeper Zeljko Kalac plans to play for English first-division club Portsmouth have been thrown into chaos with offers coming from premier league clubs, West Ham and Everton. Kalac has always dreamed of playing overseas and now has the chance to do so in a competition that boasts clubs such as Manchester United and Liverpool. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Mark Taylor is under increased pressure to do well after a fourth-ball duck in Australia's match against Gloucestershire on their Ashes tour on Tuesday. Taylor's position as Australian captain is seen as unsustainable if he does not begin to show some form. Page 46.

Nova Peris-Kneebone is in London training for her first big meet as an Australian athlete. The former Australian women's hockey player will train with a squad of English athletes in the lead-up to the world track and field championships being held in Athes in August. Page 46.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker will meet with Queensland and New South Wales State of Origin coaches Paul Vautin and Tommy Raudonikis today, in a bid to quell fears of violence in tonight's State of Origin clash. Inflammatory remarks have flowed from both the players and coaches in recent days, and the ARL is concerned tonight's match may erupt into a brawl. Page 46.
THE AGE

Australian tennis star Mark Philippoussis faced, and won, the first five-set match of his career, winning first-round match at the French Open against Swede Niklas Kulti. The game took two hours 44 minutes before the Scud finished the match with three aes. Page B14.

Australian Football League side Geelong has come out in support of the games' umpires, after harsh criticism by the AFL umpires director Bill Deller. Geelong football manager Paul Armstrong said he would recommend to the AFL that umpires should only be allowed to umpire one match per round, and that recent criticism of the umpiring should not be allowed. Page B15.

In the wake of crowd disturbances in the soccer match between Sydney United and South Melbourne, where some members of the crowd lit flares at the scoring of the first goal, it has been confirmed the two clubs were threatened with expulsion from the league. Page B16.
THE HERALD SUN

Carlton veteran Justin Madden is under increased pressure with rumours the club wants the 36-year-old to retire and make way for younger blood. It is believed Madden may be dumped for rookie Mark Porter, but Madden's manager confirmed the champion ruckman is not thinking of retirement. Page 80.

Collingwood rover Tony Francis is in doubt for this weekends match against Hawthorn after it was revealed he has an ankle ligament injury. The club had been secretive about Francis' injury after he was selected three weeks in a row, and not played. Page 7.

Australian basketball player Chris Anestey has passed up the opportunity to be present at the NBA's draft in North Carolina, and has decided to stay at home and play for the Melbourne Magic in its match against Sydney. Anestey said the decision was a hard one to make, but he put his team mates first. Page 74.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian bowler Glenn McGrath has explained his reasons for making a one-fingered gesture to the Lord's crowd during an ashes tour match on Monday. He says he doesn't normally respond to the crowd in a such a way, but he lost his temper when the English fans heckled him about his bad bowling. Page 72.

Betting on Sydney race meetings is lagging A$65 million behind the relative figures for last year, a drop of almost 11 per cent, with punters preferring to bet on inter-state races. TAB marketing manager Ken Page said the trend must be of concern to the New South Wales administrators. Page 70.

South Africa and Australia will join forces at this week's SANZAR meeting to lobby for the Super 12 series to be increased to a Super 14 or 15. It is rumoured South Africa will support Australia's bid to include a Perth team in the competition, if Australia supports South Africa's bid to include Western Province. Page 66.
